amendments.text:
LOD-MUSIC-SURGE-005 — Musical identity and composition authority
Surge XT supplies a coherent project-owned virtual-analog dance workstation offline. The author's eight Music Blocks, six authored roles, 1,402 curated phrases, 170,860 notes, D Dorian and canonical 130 BPM remain the score. Acid must exhibit substantial filter movement over held notes. Nine logical voices use custom readable patches; Hat has closed/open articulations. Phrase succession retains cadence/root, energy, source adjacency and recent-three avoidance, with fresh presentation entropy on genuine returns. No factory presets, unrelated replacement compositions, live note mutations, synthetic fill replacement, +6% tempo slew or +22-cent pitch expression are required. Those previous implementation details are superseded by stable rendered phrase playback. The +8% critical-combat gain remains.

LOD-MUSIC-SURGE-006 — Playback and lifecycle
The existing server MusicDirector remains the sole authority for default-Off permission, pressure, frozen floor assignment, staging/maze continuity, stairs, bosses, accepted once-only fanfare receipts, post-victory Chill and private new-block announcements. Options On grants server permission only for the listen-server host or superadmin; opening Options changes no state, ordinary demand cannot grant permission, and local Off stays personal. Client composition requests whole validated bundled Ogg phrases via bounded lazy native playback. Music Off/zero volume releases active music/bridge/pending resources; uncancellable native opens are reserved and stopped when their stale callbacks return. Missed musical time is discarded, never replayed rapidly; each lane can start at most one phrase per intended boundary/frame. A late preparation is discarded and resynchronized to a future bar. No runtime Surge/VST, live primary note synth, external music server or soundtrack HTTP service is required. Persistent backend failure yields diagnostics/backoff and silence; it cannot hide forever behind a bridge. Legacy primary oscillator/tone engines are superseded.

LOD-MUSIC-SURGE-001 — Author-authorized MS2 rendering authority
Surge XT is an external offline authoring/build dependency. It renders the existing eight Music Blocks, six roles and 1,402 curated D-Dorian phrases at canonical 130 BPM into bundled stereo Ogg audio. Players require no synthesizer plugin, native Surge binary, MIDI installation, external music server or soundtrack HTTP service. This rule supersedes prior streamed-score and primary live-oscillator implementation rules.
LoD owns reproducible parameter manifests for nine logical voices: Acid, Industrial, Strings, Brass, Bass, Tom, Snare, Kick and Hat (closed/open articulations). All share a gritty virtual-analog dance-synth vocabulary. Acid is monophonic with resonant low-pass envelope, glide, velocity articulation and substantial continuous cutoff modulation over held notes. No factory presets supply the bank.
MusicDirector remains server authority for permission, pressure, floor/block assignment, staging, boss and accepted victory receipts. Client phrase selection retains the curated cadence/energy graph and recent-phrase avoidance. Shared fixed-tempo phrase lanes preserve reversible equal-power stair blending; role changes are musically quantized. Missed musical time is discarded, never rapidly replayed; late preparation resumes at a future boundary. One bounded rendered bridge may cover a genuine gap, with persistent failure reported.
Per-note swing/gate/timbre mutation, synthesized fills, countdown tempo lift and the 22-cent critical pitch lift are superseded implementation details. Canonical tempo stays fixed; the cheap critical-combat gain expression remains. Server master defaults Off, local opt-out/volume persist, authorized host/superadmin Options On enables the master, and opening Options changes no state. Off/zero volume releases active and pending playback. Fanfare stays once-only, with no late/spent replay and configured Chill continuation. Die Logger announces only a genuinely new block, never phrases or tension changes.
Resource tuning is bounded lazy local preparation, never whole-library decoding. Record measured encoded size and the final channel/preload/PCM/timing bounds with the implementation checkpoint. Ordinary CI validates committed assets/hashes/catalog/durations and scheduler/lifecycle regressions; full bank regeneration separately requires the pinned Surge source and Python bindings. Native Garry's Mod musical quality, timing and Steam Deck performance remain human acceptance gates. Publication to Workshop and VPS deployment remain separate actions.

LOD-MUSIC-SURGE-TUNING — Final bounded implementation values
Offline stable source: Surge XT release_xt_1.3.4, commit f7b97c682ade0b87da85ca5968b63d5c7c98e68d; external GPL-3.0-or-later build tool. Project parameter/renderer/binding provenance lives under tools/music/surge and docs/MS2_SURGE_BANK.json. Render at 44.1 kHz stereo, 32-frame MIDI timing precision, fixed 130 BPM, eight-beat loops/twelve-beat fanfare, 550 ms release allowance, fixed per-instrument gain and restrained 27 Hz high-pass/11.5 kHz low-pass. Ogg Vorbis quality 2; selected runtime encoded budget 60,000,000 bytes, design-review boundary 100,000,000 bytes. Intermediate PCM is ignored build material. Every output is actually decoded and measured in the full authoring gate. Normal CI checks committed assets/provenance/durations and does not build Surge.
Runtime: two wanted floor lanes plus at most two retiring lanes; four-beat role/resync grid; 25 ms control pump, one-second lookahead, 60 ms late-start tolerance, 700 ms gain fade, 1.2-second lane retirement. Native hard limits: eight channels including reserved/cancelled opens, two asynchronous opens, conservative 32 MiB float-PCM admission. Each floor lane has one current phrase, one retiring tail and at most one upcoming preparation. Phrase/bridge volume writes are bounded to 30 Hz. One tonal D/A bridge fades in only after a 150 ms gap, at ten percent master gain, and stops at eight seconds of persistent failure. Error retry backoff is ten seconds. Lua retains at most four arrangement metadata payloads and no decoded note pages; no all-bank audio preload is allowed. Critical-combat expression is +8% phrase gain with native master clamp 0–1. Exact measured bank/file statistics are in the committed manifest and performance record. Native GMod/Steam Deck/co-op timing, subjective timbre and performance remain human acceptance gates.
